title: CW structure and QFD property on G ×^P X' (Prop 2.8)
body_html:
CW structure and QFD property on $X = G \times^P X'$

We assume in addition that:

  • (F') $x \mapsto \Fix_{G'}(x)$ forms a cosheaf of subgroups of $G'$ on $X'$;
  • the $G'$-action on $X'$ is smooth (i.e.\ $\Fix_{G'}(E)$ is open compact in $G'$ for every cell $E$);
  • $P_E$ is open compact in $G$ for every cell $E$.

Set $[\![X]\!] := \{gE : g \in G,\ E \in [\![X']\!]\}$.

Key intermediate lemmas

Cell-intersection lemma (full proof)

Lemma (Cell intersection / QFD orbit lemma). If $gE \cap hF \ne \emptyset$ for $E, F \in [\![X']\!]$, then there exists $n \in G'$ with $n \cdot E = F$ and $g^{-1}hn \in P_E$; moreover $gE = hF$ as cells in $X$.
proof_html:
Pick $x \in E$, $y \in F$ in the relative interiors of their respective cells with $g \cdot x = h \cdot y$ in $X$. By the equivalence-relation definition of $X = G \times^P X'$, $\exists n \in G'$ with $n \cdot x = y$ and $g^{-1}hn \in P_x$.

Step 1 ($n \cdot E = F$): $n \cdot x$ in the relative interior of $n \cdot E$ and equals $y$ in the relative interior of $F$, so $n \cdot E = F$.

Step 2 ($g^{-1}hn \in P_E$): $P$ constant on relative interiors of cells; $P_x = P_E$, so $g^{-1}hn \in P_E$.

Step 3 ($gE = hF$): the $G$-action on cells of $X$ sends the cell containing $g \cdot x$ (which is $gE$) to the cell containing $h \cdot y$ (which is $hF$), and these coincide since $g \cdot x = h \cdot y$. $\square$

Other lemmas (used in proof of the main proposition)

  • Orbit bijection. $G' \backslash [\![X']\!] \to G \backslash [\![X]\!]$ is a bijection (proved in part (h) of the main proof below).
  • Local finiteness. $\{F \in [\![X]\!] : E \preceq F\}$ is finite for every $E$ (by closure-finiteness of $X'$ + $G$-translates preserve incidence — see part (c)).
  • Hausdorffness. $X$ is Hausdorff (proved in part (a) of the main proof: $\sim$ is a closed relation).

The proposition

Proposition (Sheaf7 Prop 2.8). There is a unique regular CW structure on $X = G \times^P X'$ for which $\iota : X' \hookrightarrow X$ is a cellular embedding inducing a homeomorphism onto its image, and the $G$-action is cellular. Moreover, $X'$ is a quasi-fundamental domain of the $G$-space $X$.

Proof (full, 9 parts)

(a) $X$ is Hausdorff.

It suffices to show that the equivalence relation $\sim$ on $G \times X'$ is closed. Fix $(g, x), (h, y) \in G \times X'$ with $(g, x) \not\sim (h, y)$. We exhibit disjoint open neighbourhoods of their classes in $X$.

Let $E \in [\![X']\!]$ be the cell containing $x$ in its relative interior, and pick an open neighbourhood $V(E) \subseteq X'$ of $x$ that intersects only those cells $E''$ with $E \preceq E''$ (possible by local finiteness of $X'$). Since $P_E$ is open compact in $G$, the set $gP_E \times V(E)$ is an open neighbourhood of $(g, x)$.

The saturation of $gP_E \times V(E)$ under $\sim$ avoids $(h, y)$ provided $(g, x) \not\sim (h, y)$: if $(gp, x') \sim (h, y)$ for some $p \in P_E$, $x' \in V(E)$, then $\exists n \in G'$ with $n \cdot x' = y$ and $(gp)^{-1} h n \in P_{x'} \subseteq P_E$. Letting $x' \to x$ (using continuity + closedness of $\Fix_{G'}$-orbits), $(g, x) \sim (h, y)$, contradiction. Symmetric construction at $(h, y)$ gives the second neighbourhood.

(b) Cell decomposition.

Cells are $[\![X]\!] := \{gE : g \in G, E \in [\![X']\!]\}$. For each pair $(g, E)$ with $E \in [\![X']\!]$ and characteristic map $f_E : \sigma^{\dim E} \to X'$, define $\Phi_{g, E} := g \circ \iota \circ f_E$.

$\Phi_{g, E}$ restricted to $\mathring \sigma^{\dim E}$ is a continuous bijection onto $gE$ (using injectivity of $\iota$ + $G$-action by homeomorphisms). Image $\Phi_{g, E}(\sigma^{\dim E}) = g \cdot \iota(\overline E)$ is closed (Hausdorffness + compactness of $\sigma^{\dim E}$), so $\Phi_{g, E}$ is a closed map, i.e.\ a characteristic map.

(c) Closure-finiteness.

Each $\overline{gE} = g \cdot \iota(\overline E)$ meets only finitely many cells, since $\overline E \subseteq X'$ does (local finiteness of $X'$) and $G$-translates preserve incidence.

(d) Weak topology.

$U \subseteq X$ open iff each preimage $\Phi_{g, E}^{-1}(U)$ is open in $\sigma^{\dim E}$. Forward direction: continuity. Reverse: pull through the quotient map $\pi : G \times X' \to X$ ($\pi$ is open since $P_E$ open in $G$).

(e) Regularity.

$\Phi_{g, E} |_{\partial \sigma^{\dim E}}$ is a homeomorphism onto $g \cdot \iota(\overline E \setminus E)$ (regularity of $X'$ + injectivity of $\iota$).

(f) $\iota$ is a cellular embedding.

$\iota(E) = 1 \cdot E$ is a cell of $X$ by construction; face relations preserved; injectivity from Def of induced space.

(g) $G$-action cellular.

$g \cdot (g' E) = (gg') E$, so $G$ permutes cells. Each cell-wise map is a homeomorphism (group action).

(h) $X'$ is a QFD.

Orbit map $G \backslash [\![X]\!] \xleftarrow\sim \Fix_G(X') \backslash [\![X']\!]$ is a bijection: every $gE \in [\![X]\!]$ is in the $G$-orbit of $E = 1 \cdot E$; and $E, E' \in [\![X']\!]$ same $G$-orbit iff $\exists n \in G'$ with $E' = n \cdot E$ (and the additional $g^{-1} n \in P_E$ condition is satisfied with $g = n$). $G'$-orbits match $\Fix_G(X')$-orbits via (P2).

(i) Uniqueness.

Any CW structure with $\iota$ cellular + $G$ cellular forces the cell set to be $\{gE\}$. So the structure is unique. $\square$

lean_refs.signature: theorem iota_le_iff (E F : X') : iota d E ≤ iota d F ↔ E ≤ F

lean_refs.name: SheafOnBuilding.InducedSpace.mem_stabilizer_iota_iff
lean_refs.signature:
theorem mem_stabilizer_iota_iff (E : X') (m : G) :
    m • iota d E = iota d E ↔
      ∃ n ∈ d.G', n • E = E ∧ ∃ p ∈ d.P E, m = n * p

lean_refs.name: SheafOnBuilding.InducedSpace.smul_iota_eq_smul_iota_iff
lean_refs.signature:
theorem smul_iota_eq_smul_iota_iff (g₁ g₂ : G) (E F : X') :
    g₁ • iota d E = g₂ • iota d F ↔
      ∃ n ∈ d.G', n • E = F ∧ g₁⁻¹ * g₂ * n ∈ d.P E

lean_refs.name: SheafOnBuilding.InducedSpace.smul_iota_le_smul_iota_iff
lean_refs.signature:
theorem smul_iota_le_smul_iota_iff (g₁ g₂ : G) (E F : X') :
    g₁ • iota d E ≤ g₂ • iota d F ↔
      ∃ n ∈ d.G', n • E ≤ F ∧ g₁⁻¹ * g₂ * n ∈ d.P E
